title: Water Network in the Binding Pocket of Fluorinated BPTI-Trypsin Complexes - Insights from Simulation and Experiment
authors: Leon Wehrhan; Jakob Leppkes; Nicole Dimos; Bernhard Loll; Beate Koksch; Bettina G. Keller
one_liner_zh: 该文通过MD模拟和晶体学实验研究氟化BPTI-胰蛋白酶复合物结合口袋中水网络对结合亲和力的影响，属于广义蛋白-蛋白互作体系，但非TF-DNA，且方法为MD模拟，可迁移至蛋白-DNA界面水分子研究，故评5分。
abstract: Structural waters in the S1 binding pocket of β -trypsin are critical for the stabilization of the complex of β -trypsin with its inhibitor bovine pancreatic trypsin inhibitor (BPTI). The inhibitor strength of BPTI can be modulated by replacing the critical lysine residue at the P1 position by non-natural amino acids. We study BPTI variants in which the critical Lys15 in BPTI has been replaced by α -aminobutyric acid (Abu) and its fluorinated derivatives monofluoroethylglycine (MfeGly), difluoroethylglycine (DfeGly) and trifluoroethylglycine (TfeGly). We investigate the hypothesis that additional water molecules in the binding pocket can form specific non-covalent interactions to the fluorinated side chains and thereby act as an extension of the inhibitors. We report potentials of mean force (PMF) of the unbinding process for all four complexes and enzyme activity inhibition assays. Additionally, we report the protein crystal structure of the Lys15MfeGly-BPTI- β -trypsin complex (pdb: 7PH1). Both, experimental and computational data, show a step-wise increase in inhibitor strength with increasing fluorination of the Abu side chain. The PMF additionally shows a minimum for the encounter complex and an intermediate state just before the bound state. In the bound state, the computational analysis of the structure and dynamics of the water molecules in the S1 pocket shows a highly dynamic network of water molecules that does not indicate a rigidification or stabilizing trend in regards to energetic properties that could explain the increase in inhibitor strength. The analysis of the enthalpy and the entropy of the water molecules in the S1 binding pocket using Grid Inhomogeneous Solvation Theory confirms this result. Overall, fluorination systematically changes the binding affinity but the effect cannot be explained by a persistent water network in the binding pocket. Other effects, such as the hydrophobicity of fluorinated amino acids and the stability of the encounter complex as well as the additional minimum in the potential of mean force in the bound state, likely influence the affinity more directly. abstract_zh: β-胰蛋白酶S1结合口袋中的结构水对于β-胰蛋白酶与其抑制剂牛胰蛋白酶抑制剂（BPTI）复合物的稳定性至关重要。BPTI的抑制剂强度可通过将P1位置的关键赖氨酸残基替换为非天然氨基酸来调节。我们研究了BPTI变体，其中BPTI中的关键Lys15被α-氨基丁酸（Abu）及其氟化衍生物单氟乙基甘氨酸（MfeGly）、二氟乙基甘氨酸（DfeGly）和三氟乙基甘氨酸（TfeGly）所替代。我们探究了以下假设：结合口袋中的额外水分子能与氟化侧链形成特异性非共价相互作用，从而作为抑制剂的延伸部分发挥作用。我们报告了所有四种复合物解离过程的平均力势（PMF）以及酶活性抑制实验。此外，我们还报告了Lys15MfeGly-BPTI-β-胰蛋白酶复合物的蛋白质晶体结构（pdb：7PH1）。实验和计算数据均显示，随着Abu侧链氟化程度的逐步增加，抑制剂强度也逐步增强。PMF还显示了遭遇复合物的最小值以及结合态前的一个中间态。在结合态中，对S1口袋中水分子结构和动力学的计算分析显示，水分子网络具有高度动态性，并未表明在能量性质方面存在刚性化或稳定化趋势，这无法解释抑制剂强度的增加。使用网格非均匀溶剂化理论对S1结合口袋中水分子的焓和熵进行分析，证实了这一结果。总体而言，氟化系统地改变了结合亲和力，但该效应不能通过结合口袋中持久的水网络来解释。其他效应，如氟化氨基酸的疏水性、遭遇复合物的稳定性以及结合态中平均力势的额外最小值，可能更直接地影响亲和力。TOC图形
